localities.name: Unincorporated Los Angeles County
localities.covers: Work performed in unincorporated areas of the county — not inside any incorporated city. Most of the county's population lives in a city with its own rate; check your worksite address.

facts.summary: Unincorporated Los Angeles County sets its own minimum wage of $18.47 an hour from 1 July 2026, above both the California and federal floors. It applies to everyone working in an unincorporated area regardless of immigration status, employer size, or where you live.
facts.sourceAgency: Los Angeles County Dept of Consumer & Business Affairs
facts.notes: Adjusts each 1 July by the Los Angeles-area CPI-W. Compiled from the agency's published rate via web search; the agency page could not be fetched directly from this environment, so re-confirm before counsel review.

localities.name: City of Los Angeles
localities.covers: Work performed inside Los Angeles city limits — at least two hours in a week. Separate, higher rates apply to large hotels.

facts.summary: The City of Los Angeles sets its own minimum wage of $18.42 an hour from 1 July 2026. Note this is slightly below the unincorporated county rate — which of the two you are owed depends on whether your worksite is inside the city.
facts.sourceAgency: Los Angeles Office of Wage Standards

facts.summary: Hotels with 60 or more guest rooms (50 or more near the airport) must pay a $25.00 cash wage from 1 July 2026, plus $4.25 an hour toward health benefits — or $29.25 an hour in total if the employer provides no qualifying health benefits.
facts.citation: Los Angeles Citywide Hotel Worker Minimum Wage Ordinance
